title: Risk Capital is tranched into Junior and Senior layers with a hard sequential waterfall, not pro-rata sharing
content:
A.3.2.1.2.2 splits Total Risk Capital "into two categories based on loss absorption seniority: Junior Risk Capital (JRC) and Senior Risk Capital (SRC), further divided by source."

The waterfall is absolute in both directions. A.3.2.1.2.2.1: JRC "is the first capital to absorb losses ... Junior Risk Capital must experience 100% losses before any losses are absorbed by Senior Risk Capital." A.3.2.1.2.2.2: SRC "only begins to absorb losses after Junior Risk Capital has experienced 100% losses and absorbs 100% of losses thereafter." There is no shared band and no partial subordination.

What this buys is the ability to sell risk exposure to parties with different appetites out of the same pool of underlying investments. A.3.2.1.2.2.2.1.2 defines External Senior Risk Capital as capital "provided from the srUSDS smart contract, which allow users to provide USDS to Sky Core to serve as senior risk capital in exchange for higher returns" — retail-accessible tranched exposure to Prime Agent performance, protected by the full junior layer beneath it. A.3.2.1.2.2.2.1.1 supplies the internal counterpart, Internal Senior Risk Capital sourced from Aggregate Backstop Capital.

The structure also lets both layers be sourced *between* Agents: SRC can be originated from Sky Core monthly through the Monthly Settlement Cycle or rented from other Prime Agents via the Risk Capital Rental Primitive, exactly as junior capital can. Seniority is a property of the claim, independent of who supplied it.

The tradeoff of a clean waterfall is cliff behaviour: senior providers are perfectly safe until the junior layer is exactly exhausted, then fully exposed. That concentrates all of the incentive value of the structure in whoever holds the junior tranche — which is why the junior layer has its own internal allocation rules rather than being treated as one homogeneous pool.
description: Junior Risk Capital must take 100% losses before Senior absorbs anything, after which Senior absorbs 100% — letting Sky sell protected senior exposure via srUSDS while Agents stay first in line.
